newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cousteau's memories to be published posthumously.
newsitem.headline: Cousteau's memories to be published posthumously.

text.p: French oceanographer Jacques-Yves Cousteau summed up his adventures and warnings against harming the environment in a book to be published on Tuesday, less than a week after he died.
His widow Francine said the book, "The Man, the Octopus and the Orchidea", was the testament to Cousteau who died on Wednesday at the age of 87.

Paris publisher Robert Laffont said Cousteau wrote the book over the course of 20 years, combining personal memories and anecdotes of life aboard his ship Calypso with philosophical and political thoughts.
It said it was "the powerful book of a perpetual rebel" providing deep reflection on our present and future.

Robert Laffont said the adventures of the Calypso crew formed the background to a strong condemnation of modern environmental hazards -- industrial fishing depleting the oceans, military and civilian use of nuclear energy, destruction of the ozone layer, and deforestation.
